author: arshpatankar
description:
Hi HN! We’re Arsh and Max, founders of Axonnic (https://axonnic.com). We’ve developed a forearm sleeve that reads muscle activity to decode finger movements and estimate fingertip force, while leaving the hands bare. It’s used to record human movement and generate training data for dextrous robots.

Here’s a demo video: https://youtube.com/shorts/xBrocTc9cfA

We’ve found that electromyography (EMG) is a much better way to train robots than by video alone because video only captures movement, not muscle activity or the effort behind the movement. A useful signal can be present even when the hand barely moves; just maintaining a grip involves muscle activation. The subtle muscle movements that can barely be picked up in video are the most important details for activities like sewing and delicate assembly.

The sleeve has 64 channels of surface electromyography, or EMG. Electrodes
title: Launch HN: Axonnic (YC F26) – Sleeves that track fingers and estimate force

description: Hi HN, I am Tigran (github.com/tigranbs) I made Fakemetrics.com as a fun experiment while testing how well Claude Opus can build pixel-identical UIs. It turned out it wasn't as easy as just prompting it, but I spent time building the system so it works almost every time. And I am pretty sure you are seeing a bunch of people posting weekend vibe-coded apps and saying "$50K/month after quitting my McDonnalds job...". Well, even my friend tried to fake it a few months back. So, I kinda did this fakemetrics.com as an experiment to see how well I can have the system that clones UIs, and packaged that as a very simple (I think) usable product for the people that want to be a superstar "build in public" type of a person with no revenue, but a perfect Stripe user growth screenshot. Useful? - Probably not that much Fun? - YES!! The best part is that Claude, ChatGPT, or Grok models aren't that good at UI clones by default, but with fakemetrics.com I kinda made a system that produces near-ide
title: Show HN: Fakemetrics.com – "build in public" like a superstar

description:
A lot of people outside tech ask me if AI is going to replace programmers and I just think: if that were the case we should be running out of things to do

The bug backlog should be empty and we've caught up to every feature request from PMs to the point that we are bottlenecked on the business side

But that does not seem to be the case with my own company or most devs I talk to in the industry

So what gives?

author: jcs
description:
Hi HN, I'm James, one of the co-founders of Coral.

Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway that sits between your agents and the systems they work on. Agents call tools by writing short TypeScript programs that they can save as custom tools to reuse.

You can publish custom tools for groups of agents, so your team’s library of tools adapts to your unique systems, data and use cases. Custom tools help agent performance and give more precise units of permission control.

Here’s a short demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p0PKOlHLyVI

We started on this while building an AI SRE. To investigate an incident, the agent had to connect the dots across an ocean of telemetry data and undocumented relationships across internal and external systems. It took broad permissions, a lot of tokens and it would start from scratch the next time.

We built Coral so that the agent remembers the route. Once a task succe
title: Show HN: Coral – Open-source gateway where agents write their own tools
